lean.statement: For every finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space E, measurable probability space (Omega,mu), finite node type iota, C2 potential V with kappa>=1 and kappa^(-1)||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=||v||^2, parameters 0<eta<=c<1 and eps>0, measurable X,P with integrable E[||X-xstar||^2+||P||^2]<=M and gradient V xstar=0, nodes |t_i|<=1, measurable innovations G_j with integrable E||G_j||^2<=finrank(E), and weights with sum_j |omega_ij|<=S, let Y0_i=X+t_i P and B=6M+3eps^2+3eta finrank(E). There exist measurable p:E->E, N:E->Nat and q:E->E such that p(y)+eta gradient V(p(y))=y, ||q(y)-p(y)||<=eps, the finite proximalQuery interpreter returns some(q(y),N(y)+1), and, writing Z0_j=gradient V(q(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta)G_j) and Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j, every displayed squared gradient is integrable and E||gradient V(Y0_i)||^2<=2M, E||Z0_j||^2<=B, and E||gradient V(Y1_i)||^2<=4M+2S^2B.
approved_definition_context: All expectations are real Bochner integrals under the displayed probability measure. Integrable is asserted separately for every squared norm before its integral inequality is used.
gradient is the real inner-product gradient. ContDiff R 2 makes the displayed totalized Frechet derivatives genuine. finrank(E) is the real dimension after coercion.
proximalQuery is the existing exact-real finite-fuel interpreter: its successful result records the returned point and the number of gradient tests, including success.
The finite sum is over all nodes. No independence or Gaussian-distribution predicate occurs in the statement; only measurable innovations with the displayed marginal second-moment bound are assumed.
The variables p,N,q may depend on V,kappa,eta,c,eps and the ambient structures, but not on the probability-space realization w.
